prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold storage, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns. Goals: timeliness, pharmacist oversight, traceability, clinical control.

Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer.

Elements:
- Medication Order Gateway: validates orders from authorized clinical systems; flags missing/duplicate/conflicting data; routes to pharmacy; sends order status; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot.
- Pharmacy Verification Station: displays queue/validation; final verification; audit record.
- Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot: prepares authorized orders only; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag.
- Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler: temperature logging, excursion/connectivity-loss reports.
- East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles: route deliveries via Pneumatic Tube Network; East monitors capsules, records route/timing/status; sends Tube Route Exception Ticket on route deviation or timeout.
- North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers: report availability; block dispensing when Out of Service.
- Medication Return Kiosk: produces Return Bin Audit Label.

Actors:
- Clinical Pharmacist: clinical review; judges suitability of storage/delay-affected stock; produces Dose Exception Review Slip.
- Pharmacy Technician: prep, discrepancy clarification, cooler checks; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card; verifies capsule contents/order IDs before re-delivery.
- Medication Safety Officer: trends; produces Diversion Review Packet.
- Charge Nurse: informs staff of delays/workarounds; sends Cabinet Downtime Notice; confirms staff notified before restoring cabinet.
- Registered Nurse: confirms ongoing need; follows contingency on delay.
- Biomedical Engineer: inspects tube hardware/switches/sensors, cabinet hardware; verifies post-repair.
- IT Operations Specialist: console/controller connectivity, interfaces, logs.
- Dispatch personnel: hold capsules, block faulted routes. Operations staff: queue review, alternate routes, authorize resumption. Hospital Courier: manual transport.

Modes: route Faulted/Available; cabinet Out of Service/Normal (controlled downtime).

Rules: discrepancies block prep; final verification before release; excursion stock and returns segregated pending disposition; tube segment unavailable until tested safe; dispatch resumes only after checks and operations authorization; ward contingency maintains accountability via authorized dispensing location; technical staff document fault, corrective action, verification in service record.

Document units:
S072: A cabinet remains unavailable until its controller reports Ready for Dispense and required operational checks are complete.
S073: Operations closes the interruption only after staff confirm that dispensing and delivery workflows are functioning as intended.
S074: Final pharmacy release occurs only after the order, prepared medication, and intended destination have been checked against the approved dispensing instructions.
S075: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical and labeling exceptions that require professional judgment before authorizing release.
S076: The Pharmacy Technician confirms that the package contents and patient identifiers match the verified order.
S077: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot presents the completed package at the Pharmacy Verification Station for the final check.
S078: The Pharmacy Verification Station records the verification outcome and prevents release while required checks remain incomplete.
S079: The Pharmacy Verification Station produces the Batch Release Note after the final release checks are recorded.
S080: The release decision is associated with the order identifier, package identifier, verification time, and responsible staff credentials.
S081: The Medication Order Gateway provides the current order status used to confirm that the request remains valid.
S082: A canceled, duplicated, or superseded request is held for resolution rather than placed into a delivery load.
S083: The Clinical Pharmacist documents the disposition of any clinical concern before the package can proceed.
S084: Supporting records are prepared before a load enters the delivery network so staff can establish what was released and under which conditions.
S085: The load manifest identifies each package, its intended destination, handling requirements, and the time it was assembled.
S086: Package identifiers are checked against the manifest to detect omissions, substitutions, or duplicate entries.
S087: Temperature-sensitive packages remain under controlled conditions until their custody is formally transferred.
S088: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temperature conditions while medication awaits transfer.
S089: At the physical handoff, the Hospital Courier checks package count, packaging integrity, destination information, and any special handling instructions.
S090: The courier records the time and identity associated with acceptance so the custody history remains traceable.
S091: The Hospital Courier produces the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record when the capsule is sealed for transfer.
S092: The courier verifies that the capsule is closed securely and that its contents are not exposed during handling.
S093: The Pneumatic Tube Network accepts only loads that meet the applicable packaging and routing requirements.
S094: The East Tube Dispatch Console checks the requested route and reports whether the route is available for dispatch.
